title: "008 — First-class inference router templates"
---

## 008 — First-class inference router templates {#sec-008}

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Extend the one-click treatment from direct providers to inference routers —
services fronting many upstream models behind one endpoint: a curated coding-agent
gateway with a free tier, self-hosted LiteLLM, a zero-markup hosted gateway, and an
EU-endpoint router — alongside the existing OpenRouter and Kilo Gateway entries.

**Why.** Companion research identified four high-audience routers users could only reach
via manual custom endpoints. LiteLLM mattered doubly: it is the de-facto self-hosted
gateway of Mayon's audience, and the sanctioned path to enterprise-cloud models — cloud
credentials stay server-side inside the user's own gateway, so Mayon ever sees only
standard wire format. Direct enterprise integrations remained explicit non-goals.

**Outcome & reversals.** Shipped in roughly half a day: four templates appended after the
direct-provider block (order tests extended, catalog grew to seventeen), more gateway URLs
added, and — the single runtime change — discovery now skips entries typed as embedding:
a conservative one-value denylist protecting discoverable providers from mixed catalogs,
provably leaving untyped catalogs unchanged. LiteLLM became the first hosted template with
no required key, reusing Ollama's keyless flow: setup completes without a key prompt,
anonymous discovery works, and a key saved later upgrades the connection. Its fallback
list ships intentionally wrong placeholders: for a private gateway, the user's own
configured aliases are the only real catalog. Documented rough edge rather than solved:
inside Mayon's containerized server, localhost resolves within the container, so docs
point self-hosted-gateway users at the docker host address — an address edit, not
auto-detection. No reversals; feature [#009](009-provider-request-settings.qmd#sec-009) routes router-prefixed model ids
through last-segment matching instead of adding router dialect rows.

**Learnings.**

- Delegation beats accumulation: one self-hosted-gateway template covers arbitrarily many
  upstreams, including clouds whose auth flows Mayon will never implement.
- Append template cohorts as contiguous demand-ordered blocks; order stays meaningful and
  tests extend instead of rewriting.
- Discovery filters should be denylists grown only on observed evidence; an allowlist
  would have emptied the many untyped catalogs.
- Keyless support is positive capability design — skip the prompt, discover anonymously,
  upgrade later.
